parts.markdown:
Use our free North Dakota paycheck calculator to estimate your take-home pay after federal income tax, North Dakota income tax, Social Security, Medicare and other employee deductions.

Enter your annual salary or hourly wage, choose your payment frequency and customize your payroll information to understand how much money you could receive on payday.

North Dakota has relatively low individual income tax rates and a substantial zero-withholding income range. Depending on your earnings and filing status, your state paycheck withholding may be small or even zero.

Whether you work in Fargo, Bismarck, Grand Forks, Minot or Williston, understanding your net earnings can help you compare employment opportunities and manage household expenses.

## How to Use the North Dakota Paycheck Calculator

Choose annual salary or hourly wages and select the pay schedule shown on your pay stub. Hourly employees can enter their regular hours and qualifying overtime.

Enter the federal and North Dakota income tax withheld for that pay period. Use the full withholding amounts, including any additional withholding.



Include employee retirement contributions, eligible health premiums and other deductions from the same pay period. Enter each deduction once.

Enter prior year-to-date taxable wages if you are approaching a Social Security or Additional Medicare threshold.

Your actual paycheck depends on taxable earnings, filing classification, employment circumstances and employee benefits.

The [North Dakota Office of State Tax Commissioner](https://www.tax.nd.gov/) publishes official employer withholding instructions.

## How North Dakota State Income Tax Works

North Dakota uses a progressive individual income tax system with three ordinary tax rates.

The zero-rate bracket allows qualifying taxable income below the applicable threshold to avoid ordinary state income tax.

Income exceeding that threshold may be subject to a 1.95% rate, while higher taxable income may be subject to a 2.5% rate.

However, employees should distinguish between annual taxable income and the annualized wage amount used in payroll withholding.

The state's employer percentage method incorporates its own withholding thresholds. These should not automatically be replaced with the brackets used to calculate an annual income tax return.


## Using North Dakota Withholding From Your Pay Stub

Use the state withholding amount for the current pay period. Your employer’s withholding may depend on your payroll frequency and the federal Form W-4 it has on file. Review the North Dakota Office of State Tax Commissioner’s employer guidance for the applicable schedule.


## North Dakota Paycheck Example: $65,000 Salary

A $65,000 salary paid biweekly gives $2,500 in gross pay. This example uses $216.15 in federal withholding and $50 in North Dakota withholding as illustrative paystub entries. Assume ordinary covered wages with federal wage thresholds still ahead and no benefit deductions.

Use the [salary-to-hourly calculator](/calculators/salary-to-hourly-calculator/) to compare offers and the [emergency fund calculator](/savings/emergency-fund-calculator/) to evaluate how much net pay you can set aside.


## Frequently Asked Questions


### Can my North Dakota withholding be zero?

Yes. Some wages fall within the applicable zero-withholding range. Enter zero if your pay stub shows no state withholding.

### Where do I find my North Dakota withholding?

Look for North Dakota income tax on the pay stub and use the amount for the current period, including any additional state withholding already deducted.

### Does take-home pay show my final tax liability?

Your take-home pay reflects payroll deductions. Your annual return determines final tax liability.
